---
title: "Part 0 — One-time setup"
---

Do this **once per computer**, before the session. Budget 20 minutes, and do
it while you have decent internet.

::: {.callout-warning}
## This part cannot be delegated to AI

Creating your account and logging in are the only steps in this tutorial that
involve your personal credentials. Claude cannot do them for you, and you
should be suspicious of any tool that offers to. Everything *after* this point
is negotiable.
:::

## 1. Install the four tools

::: {.panel-tabset}
### macOS

```bash
xcode-select --install       # installs git (and much else); skip if already done
brew install gh              # GitHub CLI
```

R and RStudio: download from [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
(install R first, then RStudio).

No Homebrew? Get `gh` from [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com).

### Windows

1. **Git** — [git-scm.com/download/win](https://git-scm.com/download/win). Accept the
   defaults. This also installs *Git Bash*, a terminal where these commands work.
2. **GitHub CLI** — [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com).
3. **R then RStudio** — [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).

::: {.callout-note}
Run the commands in this tutorial in **Git Bash** or in RStudio's *Terminal*
tab, not in PowerShell, unless you know what you are doing.
:::

### Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install git gh r-base
```

RStudio from [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
:::

## 2. Make a GitHub account

[github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup). Use an email you will still
have after you graduate. Turn on two-factor authentication when it asks —
GitHub requires it and you will be forced to eventually anyway.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Pick a username you would put on a CV
Your GitHub profile is public and outlives the course. `ulo-maivali` ages
better than `xX_stats_destroyer_Xx`.
:::

## 3. Log in from your computer

```bash
gh auth login -h github.com
```

Four prompts. Answer them like this:

| Prompt | Answer | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Preferred protocol | **HTTPS** | Simpler than SSH keys; nothing to generate or lose |
| Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials? | **Yes** | This is what makes `git push` work without ever typing a password. Do not skip it. |
| How would you like to authenticate? | **Login with a web browser** | Creates a token with only the permissions you need |
| One-time code | press Return, paste the code in the browser, authorise | |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not paste a Personal Access Token unless you have to
The browser login mints a narrow, revocable token. A hand-made "classic" token
often ends up with far more power than this course needs (organisation admin,
for instance), and it sits on your laptop for years.
:::

## 4. Tell git who you are, and how to behave

Four lines. Run them once; they apply to every project on this computer.

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Actual Name"
git config --global user.email "the-email-you-used-for-github@example.com"
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global pull.rebase false
```

Windows only, to stop line-ending noise in a mixed-OS group:

```bash
git config --global core.autocrlf true
```

Why each one matters:

`user.name` / `user.email`
: Stamped into every commit you make, forever. On macOS git will silently fall
  back to your system account name if you skip this, so your commits may end
  up authored by "Admin". Set it.

`init.defaultBranch main`
: Git's built-in default is still `master` on some versions; GitHub expects
  `main`. Mismatched names cause confusing push errors.

`pull.rebase false`
: **The most commonly skipped line, and it causes a hard failure.** Without it,
  the first time your work and your teammate's work diverge, `git pull` aborts
  with `fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches.` and eight
  lines of hints. `false` means "merge", which is the honest, safe option —
  it never rewrites history you have already shared.

## 5. Check it worked

```bash
git --version
gh auth status
git config --global --list | grep -E "user|branch|rebase"
R --version
```

You want: a git version, `✓ Logged in to github.com account <you>`, your four
config lines, and an R version. If `gh auth status` says your token is invalid,
run `gh auth login` again.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Stuck?
Paste the entire error message into Claude Code and say *"this happened while
setting up git, what do I do?"*. Pasting the **whole** message including the
hints matters — the hints usually contain the answer.
:::
